intended_object: The infinitesimal generator A x = lim_{t→0} (U(t)x − x)/t of a unitary strongly continuous one-parameter group U on a complex inner product space, taken as a complex-linear unbounded operator (a ℂ-linear partial map) on its natural domain. This is the operator in Stone's theorem; the description comes from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition passes to the forward semigroup `U.toSemigroup`. Unitarity makes that semigroup complex-linear (`IsUnitary.isComplexLinear`, proved from inner-product preservation and the group law). The definition then takes the semigroup's `complexGenerator`. That construction has the same domain as the real generator, viewed as a complex submodule (closure under complex scalars is proved), and the same values. It is the real generator with its linearity upgraded from ℝ to ℂ.

The group's real generator `U.generator` is by definition the generator of the forward semigroup. That matches the standard definition of a C₀-group's generator: the one-sided and two-sided limits give the same operator, and the library proves the two-sided limit separately. So the definition gives exactly the usual generator A, viewed as a ℂ-linear operator. The Stone generator is then defined from it as −iA, a convention the module handles separately.

Generality: the complex-linear construction already exists in full generality, for any complex-linear C₀-semigroup on a complex normed space, as `StronglyContinuousSemigroup.complexGenerator`. This declaration is just the specialisation to unitary groups used in Stone's theorem, where unitarity is exactly what supplies complex linearity. So it is not too narrow. Mathlib has no theory of C₀-semigroup generators, so there is no Mathlib counterpart.
